title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : The Four Kings were once the great leaders of a country of humans. During the Age of Fire, Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight recognized their abilities and foresight and rewarded them with a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the title of kings, using his power to bind and hold close to him the powerful humans. The god also allowed them to build their civilization of New Londo near Anor Londo as a lower vassal of the city of the gods. Over time their city of humans grew to host countless lives, becoming a robust and flourishing culture. Although at some point the First Flame began to fade out, leading to the emergence of the Curse of Undeath, the city continued to exist and function as an Undead city, implying the good governance of the four kings who managed to adapt to the change.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Unequipping the Covenant of Artorias will result in the player dying immediately; you cannot unequip this ring while fighting the Four Kings. After the battle has been completed, the ring is no longer necessary and may be unequipped without dying.
Upon entry, the player will have time to cast any sort of buffs, during which a single king will appear; the second will join 35 seconds later; the last two appearing after the next 35 seconds. It is vital to eliminate each King quickly to avoid being surrounded.
There is no obligation to kill any specific amount of kings, so it is possible to spread out the damage to several of them. This can be done by dealing massive postmortem damage to a single King, as they can still be hurt during their death animation.
Power Within adds decent amounts of damage to attacks and can help destroy individual Kings quickly before the next one appears.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The Four Kings' title uses the kanji "公王", a term that was used to define a nobleman that married a daughter of the King.
The sword used by the Four Kings was intended to be in the game, however, it was removed from the final version of the game.
The Four Kings are the only holders of a Lord Soul or Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard that are not shown in the opening cinematic.
The name of the boss may reference a group of 1980s boxing legends also known as the Four Kings. One of them, Sugar Ray Leonard, is referenced in the Rayleonard Corporation of *Armored Core 4* and *For Answer*. Ironically, however, the Four Kings are weaker when at close range.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - lore 
 lore : The Abyss is a realm of Dark born from the Dark Soul or its fragments. It's an ecosystem capable of creating life, as generated by one of the core components of the First Flame, and of expanding while slowly absorbing everything in its path; it is uninhabitable to all beings aligned with Fire including the Gods, as they require special equipment or protection to prevent corruption (both in the spiritual and physical sense). In contrast, any beings aligned with or indifferent to the Abyss (such as Humans) are able to roam it with no risk of harm or corruption.

title: Drangleic
snippet: As the First Flame continued to wane, an Abyss opened beneath Drangleic, the result of the scattered fragments of an ancient abyss and the dissipated Manus, Father of the Abyss. Coalescing again, this abyss expanded across the region and assimilated all things into its growth, with its darkness felt even by those attuned to magic in neighbouring regions. A group of Undead led by Darkdiver Grandahl, called the Pilgrims of Dark, started to make pilgrimages to what they considered holy sites and delved into the Dark Chasm, to overcome the trials that lurked in the depths to refine the darkness within them. In the heart of the abyss, the Darklurker manifested: A dark, angelic creature that manipulated darkness along with sorcery, pyromancy and miracles and demonstrated superhuman abilities.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - description 
 description : The Four Kings are humans several meters tall with profoundly changed bodies and completely gray skin. Bark-like wooden membranes spread out chaotically from their heart, where their Dark Sign once stood, almost entirely covering their chest and left arm and spreading like branches. Several root-like horns extend from their heads and their spindly legs appear to be covered in bark. They all wield an enormous but terribly distorted and segmented sword, similar to the roots of their body.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Sometime after Lord Gwyn sacrificed himself to link the fading First Flame, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe began searching for a human strong enough to become the Dark Lord capable of leading humans and usher in an Age of Dark. Kaathe eventually arrived in New Londo and managed to entice the Four Kings, powerful humans who had received a fragment of Gwyn's Lord Soul, into following his ideals, teaching them the art of Lifedrain. The Serpent's dark influence extended to their entire army: The knights of New Londo became Darkwraiths, servants of the Dark who learned the art of Lifedrain and used it to absorb humanity. The Four Kings opened an Abyss in the center of their city, with their Darkwraiths beginning to employ the Red Eye Orbs granted by Kaathe to plunder humanity and expand the reach of the Abyss.

title: Witch Beatrice
snippet:
Witch Beatrice -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Aside from being a summon-able NPC for the boss fights labeled above, Witch Beatrice has no obvious contribution to the game through either story or gameplay, although her attire can be obtained.

After defeating the Four Kings, her robes and catalyst may be found on a corpse near the Firelink Shrine shortcut at the Valley of the Drakes.

During the Four Kings boss fight, Beatrice is close to becoming a hindrance to the player as her damage-per-second does not always provide enough output to quickly kill each King. On most occasions, since having an NPC increases a boss's health, having Beatrice summoned occasionally only benefits the player with a harder fight as her accuracy issues and time gaps in-between attacks gives players a much harder time killing the Four Kings.

title: Ruin Sentinels
snippet: When entering the boss room, players are initially faced with only Ruin Sentinel Yahim on an elevated platform above the rest of the arena; Alessia will be on the ground level on the opposite side of the room, with Ricce on another elevated platform. If the player does not leave the initial platform, Alessia and Ricce will not attempt to assist Yahim, making the fight considerably easier. Once Yahim is defeated, Alessia and Ricce will join the fight, both approaching to attack the player.

title: Four Kings
snippet: A nation of humans freed from the shackles of the Darksign, and who not only began to understand the powers of their Dark Soul but had an entire army at their disposal that shared this power, represented an unparalleled threat to the gods of Anor Londo, who branded the Darkwraiths as diabolical enemies of man and of every living thing. For this reason, Artorias, one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, was sent to fight the soldiers of New Londo and was given a Silver Pendant to deflect the Dark of the Abyss in its magical forms. However this did not prove sufficient to cross the Abyss of the Four Kings, and Artorias was forced to forge a covenant with the "beasts of the Abyss", obtaining a ring that would allow him to cross the Abyss, while also cursing his Greatsword. Artorias thus became known as the "Abysswalker", and hunted the Darkwraiths, but failed to eliminate the Four Kings and thus eliminate the Abyss of New Londo.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : It is possible to reach and kill the Four Kings by killing Ingward, even if the player hasn't acquired the Lordvessel yet.
The bonfire that appears *will* allow warping to escape the Abyss, even without the Lordvessel.
**This can be used as a shortcut for far away locations, such as Anor Londo, Tomb of the Giants or Ash Lake. If the player avoids resting at other bonfires, the Abyss can be used as a "home base", warping to locations in Lordran, and returning via Homeward Bone.
Although it appears to be a black void of nothingness, the "ground" of the abyss actually floats a few meters above an unseen cobblestone floor. This can be observed by using a light source, such as the Skull Lantern or Sunlight Maggot.
Items that require hitting a surface to activate, such as Prism Stones and Carvings, will not work in the Abyss as they simply fall through the "floor".

Doing so will allow the Bearer to speak directly to the king as he was before he hollowed. Bitter and resigned to defeat, the king will council the Bearer of the Curse, warning them of the futility in seeking fire, of the dark that lies within them, and of the children of Manus, Father of the Abyss. He will tell the Bearer to seek three crowns of power, belonging to fallen kings. He will also warn the Bearer of his wife, Nashandra, revealing that she too is a child of the Abyss.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
Chosen Undead -  Dark Souls - character - the_lord_souls 
 the_lord_souls : To gain access to Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, the Chosen Undead must satiate the Lordvessel. There are several beings who possess souls powerful enough to do so: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Seath the Scaleless and the Four Kings of New Londo.

In order to defeat the Four Kings, the Chosen Undead needs to acquire the Covenant of Artorias, a ring that is kept by the Great Grey Wolf Sif. The ring allows one to traverse the dark void called the Abyss. Upon arriving in the ruins of New Londo, the Chosen Undead, with the help of Ingward, drains the flooded city, earning passage to the Darkwraiths and their masters. If the player has not yet placed the Lordvessel before defeating the Four Kings, Darkstalker Kaathe will appear in the abyss.

title: Covenant of Artorias
snippet:
Covenant of Artorias -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : Covenant of Artorias allows the player to reach the Abyss. As such, it is necessary in order to reach the Four Kings boss battle. Without wearing the ring, it is impossible to survive the fall into the Abyss. Taking off the ring during the fight with the Four Kings will cause the player to be devoured by the Abyss. Other than this, the ring has no other purpose.

The Covenant of Artorias is one of the very few rings that do not carry over to NG+; players are required to kill Great Grey Wolf Sif every playthrough to obtain the ring and beat the game. This ring, when dropped, will end up in the chest behind Kingseeker Frampt after the player has quit and reloaded the game. However, in the remaster, it will automatically be in the player’s inventory.

title: Witch Beatrice

As soon as she is summoned, staying too long outside of the fog door will allow a ghost, to the player's right if they face the fog door, to aggro the player and Beatrice and because she has no transient curses, she will be stuck firing sorceries at the ghost and remain unable to assist in the boss fight until the ghost is killed.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Each of the Kings' health is equal to a bit less than ¼ of the total bar. This means that after killing four individual Kings, the boss itself may not yet be defeated and a fifth King will spawn. This can be avoided by attacking the Kings as they are dying, which can do additional damage to the life bar.
**This is because the total boss health bar belongs to a King hidden under the arena, that is hit whenever one of the other Kings is hit (even if it is a King's dead body that is being hit). This is also what causes the Lifehunt Scythe's self-inflicted Bleeding to be applied twice whenever one of the Four Kings is hit.

title: Four Kings
snippet: Although decades have passed since New Londo was reduced to rubble and submerged, the Four Kings remained alive in their Abyss, while the Darkwraiths continued to wait and patrol the area. When a Chosen Undead was able to ring the Bells of Awakening, overcome the challenges of Sen's Fortress and reach Anor Londo, thus being rewarded with the Lordvessel, they would be guided by Kingseeker Frampt to find immense souls to fill the receptacle and link the fading First Flame to succeed Gwyn in his sacrifice. The Undead would thus have proved their strength to Ingward to open the floodgates of the city and find a way to traverse the Abyss until they reached the Four Kings, challenging and killing them to obtain the fragment of a Lord Soul which they still possessed.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - notes 
 notes : The battle arena is pitch-black with no visible features. While there are invisible walls, rarely do they create complications.
The Kings spawn in one after another at a rate of about 1 every 35-40 seconds, and all four can be present at once. If one is killed before 35 seconds elapses, another will take its place, immediately resetting the spawn timer. Kings will continue to spawn for as long as the battle lasts, unless there are already four Kings present.
Although up to four may be present during the fight, the additional kings will only become hostile after about 30-40 seconds, they will glide back and forth across the arena until the timer ends, the player engages with them, or the player wanders too far from them. The other Kings, however, are able to attack with their sword if the player is close enough, or cast magic homing missiles when the player is too far.

title: Humans
snippet:
Kaathe also manipulated the inhabitants of New Londo, where he enticed the Four Kings with the art of Lifedrain, which ancient Humans used to steal Humanity from others. The Kings too were corrupted, and New Londo was flooded —presumably by the Gods— to contain the Abyss that generated there. But despite these failures, Kaathe kept searching for a human who could become the Dark Lord, and usher in the Age of Man.

At the close of the Age of Gods, Gwyn realized that the power of the Dark Soul would wax to its utmost maximum, while the power of the other Lord Souls would fade. Fearing that the world would be ruled by the Humans, Gwyn cast himself into the First Flame, artificially extending the Age of Fire for another thousand years. At Gwyn's command, The Gods shepherded the Human race afterwards.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : The **Abyss** is a location in *Dark Souls*, as well as a storyline concept featured in all three games in the series.

The in-game location is at the heart of the New Londo Ruins, a featureless expanse where the Chosen Undead must slay the Four Kings and can encounter Darkstalker Kaathe. As a concept, "Abyss" is the name given to both a force that consumes or corrupts most forms of life, and to the areas in which it dwells; it is tied to the Age of Dark, and also gave birth to a twisted offshoot known as The Deep.

title: Key to the Seal
snippet:
Key to the Seal -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Key to the floodgates of New Londo, which seal away the Four Kings who fell to Dark.

The Sealers flooded New Londo to banish the Darkwraiths and the Four Kings. The agonizing decision was made with the realization that countless lives, and the robust culture of the city, would be lost. The victims now roam the ruins as ghosts.

title: Yulva
snippet:
Yulva -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Yulva was once a healer of New Londo, dedicating herself to curing the sick with her signature spell: Remedy.

During the rise of the corrupt Four Kings and their Darkwraith servants, she would take part in the flooding of the entire city, along with Ingward and a third unknown mage. This desperate attempt to seal the threat of the Abyss seemingly worked, but it came at the cost of the lives of many of the city's citizens and its unique culture. All three mages stayed behind after the fact, watching over the seal of the Four Kings and awaiting someone capable of finally vanquishing them. This also served as atonement for all those who were sacrificed.

title: Four Kings Sword
snippet:
Four Kings Sword -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : As the name states, this weapon was intended to be connected to the Four Kings in the New Londo Ruins, either as a dropped weapon, or as a boss soul weapon. However, as it was cut from the final release of the game, it is unknown how the player would have obtained it.

Due to its nature as cut content, the Four Kings Sword is simply 3 textures and a model in the game files. This means that it cannot effectively be added by itself with save editors or cheat softwares, since its stats do not exist. Instead an existing weapon's model has to be overridden in order to 'obtain' it, in turn making the Four Kings Sword use the overridden weapon's animations and stats. Hence, the weapon can only be seen by those who are modifying the game to use its model.

title: Four Kings

But his dark influence did not stop with the kings and, in fact, their entire army followed them. The knights of New Londo became Darkwraiths, servants of the Dark who learned the art of Lifedrain and used it to absorb humanity. As the Four Kings' were able to open an Abyss in the center of their city, their very bodies were mutated by their freed Dark Soul, and the Darkwraiths' armor transformed, too, as they began to employ the Red Eye Orbs granted by Kaathe to seek humanity and plunge further into the powers of the Dark,

title: Abyss
snippet: Knight Artorias famously traversed New Londo's Abyss and hunted the Darkwraiths therein. He was protected by the power of a magical ring, which he gained after making a covenant with the beasts there. The ring prevented him from being swallowed by the void, but it led to his sword becoming cursed. In recognition of his actions, he was awarded one of Anor Londo's treasures, a Silver Pendant that allowed him to repel Dark sorceries; eventually he traveled to Oolacile to combat the threat of Manus, the lord of the Abyss. The Four Kings and Seath the Scaleless each own a Bequeathed Shard, which differ in lore from Lord Souls as they are only fragments of Gwyn's own Lord Soul, although even these fragments remain immensely powerful.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : The Japanese description of Seath's Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard uses the term (Hepburn: *gaiseki*) 'consort kin', which is used to define a person related by marriage to the maternal clan or wife's clan of the monarch, thus stating how Seath had become part of Gwyn's family through marriage with one of the daughters of his mother. However, if interpreted differently by reading the individual kanji separately like 外 (Gai) and 戚 (Seki), it would be translated as "external relative", implying that Seath would have married any woman from Gwyn's family.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet: **While the term has a historical and cultural meaning too complex to properly convey in the context of the game's lore and the fact that one could become a "Gaiseki" even marrying a sibling or cousin of the monarch's mother or even by having the monarch marry one's daughter, it is more likely that Gwyn gave Seath one of his daughters as a gift thus allowing the dragon a more close connection to the family of the monarch.

snippet:
Farron Greatsword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Farron Greatsword is a unique two-piece weapon that caters towards quality builds leaning towards Dexterity. It is one of the lightest weapons in the ultra greatsword category, and its attacks consume very little stamina for its class. Its attacks can deal solid damage, making it a powerful weapon in the right hands.

Functioning similarly to Paired Weapons, two-handing will equip the dagger in the off-hand, yielding unique attack combos and allowing the wielder to parry with the dagger. The dagger combos can yield strong stun-locking potential, while also providing the wielder with strong offensive momentum and wide sweeping attacks. However, the inability to hold the weapon in both hands is also a crucial flaw, as all attacks performed by this weapon short of the jumping attack can be parried, a disadvantage that is not shared by any other ultra greatsword.

title: First sin
snippet: Similarly, after the Lords were successful in defeating the Ancient Dragons, Gwyn used his Soul to build a civilization above-ground, for humans to worship the gods in; allowing the Furtive Pygmy's descendants to come out of their abyssal caverns and live in the sunlight. The gods built a city of castles above this world from which to rule, and effectively made ingress impossible without great strength. However, in the stead of humanity taking the plunge into sin, it is Anor Londo, following the lead of its king. Thus - perhaps symbolic of this inversion - humankind becomes damned to eternal life instead of the persistent death of reality; and the gods of *Dark Souls* become ineffectual rulers, where systems similarly devolve into chaos in real life, but as designated by Providence.

title: First sin
snippet: The term "First Sin" is likely derived from the Judeo-Christian account of humankind's [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_sin original sin], generally agreed amongst most sects to be a base flaw in all people stemming from the original humans, Adam and Eve, partaking in the fruits of a certain tree in the Garden of Eden; the sole action God strictly forbade that they do under threat of death. This fruit opened their eyes, allowing them to see and "be as God, knowing good and evil", but in disobeying God they effectively caused humans to be branded by Him as untrustworthy and capable of sin. He then cast them out of the Garden and had them toil for their food all their lives. Most significantly, however, was that there was a second tree within the Garden that bestowed everlasting life, with God Himself saying "and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever" before casting the pair out to eventually die.

title: First sin
snippet: Such decision was originated by fear, for the darkness was potentially allmighty: the Dark Soul could be split endlessly without losing its inherent strenght, the darkness could spread and expand creating an abyss uninhabitable to those who gained their strenght from the light, and it was capable of producing life. A life that, like the humans', was not bound by the death. But at the times of the end of the War against the Dragons, the young and small civilization of the humans was not yet able to pose a significant threat, and the clan of Anor Londo was at the peak of its power: therefore, Gwyn decided to act swiftly without causing the wrath of the humans. The Pigmies were granted a city to call their own, a vassal of the realm of the gods, and their king obtained the hand of one of Gwyn's daughter, Filianore, granting a great prestige to the human nobility now able to focus on the growth and prosperity of their people in peace.

title: Four Kings
snippet: Having failed to eliminate the dark threat, an agonizing and terrible decision was made: flooding the entire land of New Londo despite the realization that countless lives and the rich culture of the country would be lost. For this task, sorcerers were called, and the feat was accomplished without even evacuating the city's civilians, sealing away the Four Kings, their Darkwraiths and the entire population with them. title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - summoning 
 summoning : Summon signs are most commonly found at the beginning of the New Londo Ruins, before crossing the bridges. Some can also be found right before the boss door.

Witch Beatrice's summon sign can be found hidden around a corner just before crossing the short bridge to the Fog Door, but only if you have already summoned her for the Moonlight Butterfly fight. It may prove more than useful if you are a light build.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Initially, it can be hard to determine how close a king is; they can appear close, when they are in fact out of reach. It's a good idea to run into a king before attacking, not only to be sure your attacks will land, but also because being close to a king can cause his attacks to miss.
Using armor with good poise (Havel's Set will be the best for this as it has good defense without using materials) while staying close to the kings will allow you to tank through the hits (as they deal significantly less damage while you are next to them) and constantly hit them. Be wary, though, as full heavy armor is extremely heavy so fat rolling or even no rolling is likely. Using Green Blossoms and the Grass Crest Shield is also recommended.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Power Within adds decent amounts of damage to attacks and can help destroy individual Kings quickly before the next one appears.
The use of Great Magic Barrier, Magic Barrier, or any equipment with high magic resistance can help, as all of their attacks deal at least partial magic damage. The Dark Hand, dropped by nearby Darkwraiths, can be used in the left hand as a shield with 80% MagDef.
The damage dealt by the Kings in NG+ is far greater than in NG, so it may prove difficult to absorb their attacks with heavy armor.
Staying close to a King will force the lower portion of the blade to hit, minimizing damage. This is true even on NG+, as getting hit by the upper section of their blade will deal heavy damage. This will also prevent it from using some magic attacks (namely, the homing shot) and the unengaged Kings tend to use melee at most distances.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Using a ranged attack and staying at around 1-1.5 roll distance away in front of the king (just within the reach of his sword) makes him rely mostly on the vertical slashes and the occasional Homing Abyss Arrow or Life Drain. The Life Drain is also easier avoided since it looks less like Wrath of the Kings at this distance then it does close up, and the player already has a head start on getting out of reach.
Their homing attacks can be deflected by using Force or Wrath of the Gods, although it is safer to avoid the attacks entirely. Due to the speed at which the King approaches, the player will become vulnerable to other attacks during the casting animation. Deflecting the large homing shot will likely be fatal, since the duration of the attack lasts a fair while and doesn't collide with anything other than the player.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Despite sharing a name with a Norse goddess, Sif's gender is unconfirmed, and is not directly stated in either the English or Japanese versions of the game.
**In translations for languages that have grammatical gender, the masculine form of "wolf" is often used when referring to Sif. In French, Sif is called *Le Grand Loup Gris*, using the masculine "loup" rather than the feminine "louve", In Spanish, Sif is called *El Gran Lobo Gris*, using the masculine "lobo" rather than the feminine "loba", In Russian, Sif is called *Великий Волк*, using the masculine "волк" rather than the feminine "волчица", In Italian, Sif is called *Il Grande Lupo Grigio*, using the masculine "lupo" rather than the feminine "lupa".
**In the strategy guide by FuturePress, Sif is referred using masculine pronouns.
Another possible naming influence is the Arabic *saif* or *sayf*, meaning "sword".

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet: If the Chosen Undead saves Sif in the Chasm of the Abyss before killing Sif in Darkroot Garden, a different cutscene will play before the fight; however this will prevent you from meeting Kaathe, because you need to place the Lordvessel and visit the Duke's Archives to access the DLC. In the cutscene, Sif will recognize the player as they approach and let out a whimper. The protagonist reaches out to pet the wolf, but Sif pulls away and howls mournfully before sadly picking up Artorias' greatsword. The fight will continue as normal after this point.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Using miracles, sorcery, or pyromancy to soften Sif up before moving in with melee attacks can also prove to be effective.
Using a summoned phantom as a decoy can make positioning oneself under Sif easier. In a party of two or more players only one should try to get under Sif, otherwise players may bump into each other when trying to dodge Sif's attacks.
Sif's attacks can be blocked, but most of them will cause a significant loss of stamina, even with a good shield. Learning Sif's attack patterns and avoiding them completely, either by dodging or simply walking out of the way, is highly recommended.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Great Grey Wolf Sif -  Dark Souls - boss - location 
 location : Sif can be found in Darkroot Garden behind large, glowing doors, guarding the grave of Artorias the Abysswalker, one of Gwyn's four knights.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Great Grey Wolf Sif -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies 
 strategies : For melee fighters, getting underneath Sif is generally the best strategy, as it makes most attacks miss the player character completely. Care must still be taken to dodge, block or move out of the way of the slam attack, though. Locking on is not always a good idea when doing this, as it can make the camera spin and make it harder to control one's position. Two-handing is more effective, as it will make the fight shorter and reduce the number of slams that need to be dodged.
For ranged characters, players can simply target-lock Sif and kite Sif backwards around the edge of the arena. Staying as far as possible away from Sif will cause most, if not all, of Sif's attacks to miss.
Using miracles, sorcery, or pyromancy to soften Sif up before moving in with melee attacks can also prove to be effective.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet: Before the player enters through the fog gate, there is a broken piece of bridge to the left that can be jumped onto. This is most easily accomplished by unequipping all gear beforehand. After reaching the bridge there is another pile of rock resting at the top that can easily be reached through jumping. When at the top, Sif will be visible. Sif will be unable to reach the player, but the player will be able to damage Sif with arrows or other ranged attacks.

It may be hard to summon a phantom before the battle, as Darkroot Garden is a PvP hotspot, allowing invasions.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Great Grey Wolf Sif -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : In Norse mythology, Sif is the golden-haired wife of the god Thor.
** The goddess Sif's name in Old Norse is pronounced /siːf/, "seef", though it is often anglicized to /sɪf/, "siff". It is also a female given name in modern day Iceland.
**The name "Sif" is believed to be a singular form derived from Old Norse *sifjar*, "connection by marriage". The modern English "sib", as in "sibling", comes from the same root, as does the German "Sippe", meaning "tribe" or, coloquially, "family".
** In *Advanced Dungeons & Dragons* sourcebook *Legends & Lore* (1984), the goddess Sif is depicted wielding a longsword and wearing white and silver. These traits are shared with the Dark Souls boss Sif.
Despite sharing a name with a Norse goddess, Sif's gender is unconfirmed, and is not directly stated in either the English or Japanese versions of the game.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
In the fight against the Chosen Undead, Sif wields the sword of Artorias, former companion who sacrificed himself in order to protect Sif.
The sword Sif carries in their mouth appears to be a replica of Artorias' sword. The sword also apparently changes size between the events of Artorias of the Abyss and the main game.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
**In the strategy guide by FuturePress, Sif is referred using masculine pronouns.
Another possible naming influence is the Arabic *saif* or *sayf*, meaning "sword".
In Japanese, Sif is named 灰色の大狼シフ (*Haiiro no Ookami Shifu*), meaning "Grey (literally "ash-colored") Wolf Sif". "Ookami", "wolf", is often written in Japanese with 狼 alone (such as in the Japanese title of the anime *Spice and Wolf*, 狼と香辛料), but here is written 大狼, also read "ookami", with the first kanji carrying the meaning "great" or "large". 大狼 is also used in the Japanese translations of *A Song of Ice and Fire* to refer to the direwolves, though in that series it is read ダイアウルフ (katakana for the English "direwolf"). The alternative reading "Dairou" for 大狼 has been suggested, but this is not attested in the game.
In the fight against the Chosen Undead, Sif wields the sword of Artorias, former companion who sacrificed himself in order to protect Sif.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Knight Artorias -  Dark Souls III - boss - abyss_sludge 
 abyss_sludge : When the player is behind Artorias, he may use his Abyss Sludge attack. This move does little damage but can stun and even knock down players with little to no poise. If timed right, the player can roll forward through the attack and get a hit on him, then immediately retreat.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: As centuries passed, the ruins of Oolacile overgrew into the "Darkroot Garden", where the remnants of the ancient Guardians of the city still patrol the area as Stone Knights. Sif survived the battle with Manus thanks to the intervention of the Chosen Undead. The wolf inherited Artorias's divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias's tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias's rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead who arrived with the intention of plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: In addition, Artorias and Sif had become trusted friends of Alvina, a white Great Feline that had lived for centuries since the early Age of Fire. After Artorias's death, Alvina founded the Forest Hunter covenant, a clan of hunters bound with the aim of protecting the Darkroot Forest where her friend rested and Sif resided from the many adventurers who invaded it to seek the tomb of the legendary knight. Alvina would try to dissuade those who ventured into the region, advising them not to seek Artorias's tomb and that his legends were only fabrications and fairy tales.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: The Abyss Watchers established dominion over Farron Keep, the swampland once known as Oolacile or Darkroot Garden. Here they closely guarded what was once the Chasm of the Abyss, the cradle of Manus and a seedbed for Abyssal beasts; these headquarters would also have been in close proximity to Artorias's tomb. The Watchers gained notoriety due to their scorched-earth approach to containing outbreaks of the Abyss, destroying kingdoms at the first sign of exposure. Nonetheless, many would enlist as their followers in a bid to partake of wolf's blood and become part of the Undead Legion.

title: Lordvessel
snippet:
Lordvessel -  Dark Souls - item - notes 
 notes : It is possible to access the Kiln of the First Flame without interacting with either Frampt or Kaathe by dropping down the opening Frampt springs from. However, doing so before placing the Lordvessel will alienate the serpents and cause both of them to leave.
It is impossible to summon any phantoms at any of the Lord Boss' (excluding the Four Kings) locations without placing the Lordvessel with Frampt or Kaathe. Bloodstains, Messages and player ghosts will appear as usual and it is possible to be summoned, but not *to* summon.
To place the Lordvessel under the guidance of Kaathe, one must first continue on to the New Londo Ruins and defeat the Four Kings in order to gain access to him.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet:
Kaathe resides in the darkness of the Abyss, but seems to be more involved in the affairs of Lordran than Frampt. Kaathe gave the Four Kings the art of lifedrain and consequently founded the Darkwraith covenant. He also seems to have tricked the residents of Oolacile into uncovering the corpse of Manus, driving him mad in the process. This sparked the spread of the Abyss, transforming the townsfolk into monstrous beings whose humanity has run wild, akin to Manus.

In the ending of Dark Lord, ten additional primordial serpents are seen, whose names are unknown. They appear to want to serve the newly-appointed Dark Lord, and possibly usher in the Age of Dark. An interesting note in this ending is that Kaathe states that both himself and Frampt will serve the Chosen Undead, disregarding any actions the player has taken before reaching this point, like placing the Lordvessel with Frampt instead of Kaathe, which would make the latter refuse to cooperate with the player, and vice-versa.

title: Lore
snippet:
Gwyn, in a final effort to save the Age of Fire, marches with a great deal of his army to the Kiln of the First Flame and sacrifices himself to link with the First Flame, turning the Kiln to ash and incinerating his entire army (making them the Black Knights, who later walk Lordran). The attempt is temporarily successful, however, as the Age of Fire was only extended for at least 1000 years. Gwyn became a Hollow and is from then on known as "Gwyn, Lord of Cinder".

The Four Kings became corrupted and were seduced by evil at some point by Kaathe after Gwyn's fall and their servants turned into Darkwraiths. In an effort to stop them New Londo was flooded with all of its population, trapping the Four Kings with their Darkwraiths in the Abyss.

Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

title: Humans
snippet: Meanwhile, in a place called Oolacile, the land of golden sorceries, humans loyal to the Gods were convinced by the Darkwraith leader named Kaathe, a primordial serpent loyal to the Pygmy, to raise up a primeval man who had been buried there. He went mad, and his Humanity bubbled over from his uncontrollable rage, mutating him into a dark monster. His Humanity overflowed and consumed the very world around him, generating another Abyss, and corrupting the citizens of Oolacile. Knight Artorias, one of the four knights of Gwyn, would be tasked to face the outbreak of the Abyss, only to be corrupted by it.

title: Witch Beatrice
snippet:
Witch Beatrice -  Dark Souls - character - locations 
 locations : Darkroot Garden – Witch Beatrice can be summoned as a phantom for the Moonlight Butterfly boss fight. Her summon sign can be found under the staircase leading up to the Moonlight Butterfly (only if the player has had hollowing reversed).
New Londo Ruins – Her summon sign is later found behind a pillar before the fog door leading to the Four Kings fight in the Abyss. The Moonlight Butterfly must be defeated with Beatrice's help for her sign to appear here. (Summoning and Challenging Moonlight Butterfly is enough, Usage of Black Separation Crystal after the fight has begun still counts as helping.)
